note: Hand-written Grade 4 Core-word content, layered over the draft so it always wins. A word appears here when the course had nothing for it, or had it at the wrong reading level, or - most often in this grade - in a sense from another unit entirely. Cast is Grade 4's own: Amal, Nora, Leo, Sami, Maya, Noah, Elena, Adam, Idris, Hana, Theo, Talia, Teacher Yasmin. Sentences are capped at 80 characters and 16 words, which is what Grade 4's own authored sets already ask a reader to handle.

absorb.childMeaning: To take in or soak up a liquid or gas.
practiceSentences: Dry soil will absorb the rain very quickly.
Which cloth can absorb the most water?
Plants absorb water through their roots.
Dark surfaces absorb more heat than pale ones.
The sponge absorbed the whole spill.

abstract.childMeaning: About ideas rather than things you can touch.
practiceSentences: Kindness is an abstract idea.
Which words in this list are abstract?
Abstract nouns name feelings and thoughts.
An abstract painting shows shapes, not objects.
Freedom is abstract; a gate is not.

accomplish.childMeaning: To succeed in doing something you set out to do.
practiceSentences: The team hoped to accomplish the task by noon.
What did you accomplish this week?
Hard work helps you accomplish your goal.
Leo accomplished more than he expected.
They accomplished the climb in three hours.

according.childMeaning: Used to say where information has come from.
according.repitchedFrom: grade 5: 'As stated or reported by a particular person or piece of information' - the word is almost never met without `to`, so the meaning should describe the job it does.
practiceSentences: According to the manual, this switch resets it.
According to Nora, the meeting starts at four.
The bridge is safe, according to the engineer.
According to the label, it holds two litres.
According to the map, the river is nearby.

account.childMeaning: A record that lets you sign in to a website with your own name.
account.repitchedFrom: grade 8, which carried two senses at once - the online profile AND 'a description of what happened'. One card teaches one sense.
practiceSentences: Amal opened an account on the reading website.
Do you need an account to watch the video?
Keep your account details private at all times.
The library account lets Leo reserve books.
Nora forgot the password for her account.

action.childMeaning: Something that a person or a thing does.
practiceSentences: Her quick action saved the falling plant.
What action will the class take next?
Every action has some kind of result.
Leo took action as soon as he saw the leak.
The film was full of action from the start.

actor.childMeaning: A person who performs a role in a play or film.
practiceSentences: The actor learned every line by Friday.
Which actor played the narrator?
A good actor makes the audience believe.
Leo wants to be an actor one day.
The actor bowed at the end of the scene.

actress.childMeaning: A woman or girl who performs a role in a play or film.
practiceSentences: The actress rehearsed her scene twice.
Who is the actress in the main role?
An actress must speak clearly on stage.
The actress remembered every single word.
Maya played the actress in our school drama.

additionally.childMeaning: As well as what has already been said.
practiceSentences: Additionally, the club meets on Thursdays.
The plan saves money; additionally, it saves time.
Additionally, every pupil received a badge.
We planted trees and, additionally, cleared litter.
Additionally, the survey covered two villages.

extraSentences: I admire the way Nora keeps trying.

admission.childMeaning: Being allowed to enter a place or join a group.
practiceSentences: Admission to the museum is free on Sundays.
What are the admission rules for the club?
The school sent an admission letter to Sami.
Admission closes at four o'clock.
Her admission to the choir made her very proud.

adventure.repitchedFrom: grade 3 - the same sense at 87 characters, with a trailing clause the word does not need.
practiceSentences: The story tells of an adventure at sea.
What adventure would you choose?
Their adventure lasted three whole days.
Every adventure begins with a first step.
The book is an adventure from start to finish.

advise.childMeaning: To tell someone what you think they should do.
practiceSentences: The coach will advise you on your running.
What would you advise a new pupil to do?
Doctors advise us to sleep eight hours.
Nora asked Teacher Yasmin to advise her.
I would advise leaving a little earlier.

agreement.childMeaning: When two or more people decide on the same thing.
practiceSentences: The class reached an agreement about the trip.
Was there agreement on the new rules?
They shook hands to show their agreement.
An agreement works only if everyone keeps it.
Nora and Sami came to a quick agreement.

alliteration.childMeaning: When several words close together begin with the same sound.
alliteration.repitchedFrom: grade 7 - the same sense at 98 characters. Its sentences ran to 110 characters, the longest inherited lines in the grade, about sustainable fashion fairs and clothing swaps.
practiceSentences: 'Silver stars shine' uses alliteration.
Where is the alliteration in this line?
Alliteration makes a slogan easy to remember.
Poets use alliteration to link words.
Nora hunted for alliteration in shop signs.

allow.childMeaning: If you allow something, you let it happen.
allow.note: Meaning kept. The mined fifth sentence repeated the fourth's construction almost word for word - both were "I allow myself ..." - so the set taught one pattern four times and a second one once.
practiceSentences: Teacher Yasmin will allow extra time for the reading test.
Does your mother allow you to walk home alone, Sami?
Please allow me to help you carry that.
I allow myself a little time to draw each evening.
The rules allow two players from each class.

alongside.childMeaning: Next to or together with something or someone.
practiceSentences: She walked alongside her younger brother.
Who sits alongside you in class?
The path runs alongside the river.
Leo worked alongside the older pupils.
Two boats moored alongside the wooden jetty.
We could walk; alternatively, we could cycle.
Alternatively, you may write a poem.
Read the chapter, or alternatively watch the film.
Alternatively, the class could vote.
Use a metaphor; alternatively, try a simile.

ancestor.childMeaning: A member of your family who lived long before you were born.
ancestor.note: Meaning kept; the Grade 5 sentences ran to 90 characters and named Grandfather, who is not in Grade 4's cast.
practiceSentences: An ancestor of mine sailed across the ocean.
Which ancestor would you most like to meet?
This ring belonged to an ancestor of Grandma.
Theo drew a family tree with every ancestor named.
Our ancestor planted the trees along this road.

angle.childMeaning: The space between two lines that meet at a point.
practiceSentences: A square has four right angles.
What angle do these two roads make?
Measure the angle with a protractor.
A sharp angle is smaller than a right angle.
The roof slopes at a steep angle.

announce.childMeaning: To tell people something important or new.
announce.note: The inherited Grade 5 meaning ended without a full stop, and its sentences ran to 91 characters - station speakers, a rocket launch, a tidiness cup.
practiceSentences: The head teacher will announce the results.
When will they announce the winning team?
Speakers announce every delay at the station.
Theo waited for his parents to announce the plan.
Announce your decision clearly to the group.
The annual sports day is in June.
Is the fair an annual event?
Annual rainfall is measured every year.
The school holds an annual concert.
An annual visit keeps the family close.

antonym.childMeaning: A word that means the opposite of another word.
antonym.note: The Grade 8 meaning was correct and arrived with no capital letter and no full stop - the third such meaning found in this grade, after `cooperate` and `announce` in unit 5.
practiceSentences: 'Hot' is an antonym of 'cold'.
What is the antonym of 'ancient'?
An antonym helps you explain a meaning.
Write an antonym beside each word.
A synonym is close; an antonym is opposite.

apologise.childMeaning: To say sorry to someone for something you did wrong.
practiceSentences: Leo went to apologise for the broken cup.
Should you apologise before or after explaining?
She was quick to apologise for her sharp words.
It takes courage to apologise properly.
Apologise sincerely, not just to end the argument.

apostrophe.childMeaning: A mark showing a missing letter or who owns something.
practiceSentences: An apostrophe shows the missing letter in 'don't'.
Where does the apostrophe go in this word?
Use an apostrophe to show that Amal owns it.
A missing apostrophe changes the meaning.
Check every apostrophe when you proofread.

appearance.childMeaning: The way somebody or something looks.
practiceSentences: The appearance of the stage changed completely.
How would you describe her appearance?
Do not judge a book by its appearance.
His sudden appearance surprised everyone.
The garden's appearance improves each spring.

application.childMeaning: A program you open on a phone or computer to do a job.
application.repitchedFrom: grade 8: 'A practical use to which something, especially knowledge, is put' - the ABSTRACT sense. This unit is about devices, where an application is an app.
practiceSentences: This application helps you learn new words.
Which application do you use for drawing?
The weather application shows rain tomorrow.
Sami downloaded a maths application last week.
An application must be updated from time to time.

approach.childMeaning: To come nearer, or a way of dealing with something.
practiceSentences: Watch the bus approach the stop slowly.
How will you approach this difficult task?
The birds fly away as we approach the nest.
Leo tried a new approach to the puzzle.
Her calm approach settled the whole group.

appropriate.childMeaning: Right or suitable for a particular situation.
practiceSentences: A light meal is appropriate before exercise.
Is this an appropriate portion for a child?
Choose clothing appropriate for hot weather.
The nurse gave appropriate advice about rest.
An appropriate snack keeps you going till lunch.

approximate.childMeaning: Close to the real amount, but not exact.
practiceSentences: Give me an approximate depth of the lake.
Is that an approximate or an exact figure?
The approximate temperature was twenty degrees.
An approximate answer is enough for this task.
Sami wrote the approximate weight in his notes.

architect.childMeaning: A person who designs buildings and structures.
architect.note: Meaning kept; two Grade 5 sentences ran past this grade's cap.
practiceSentences: An architect drew the plans for our new hall.
What does an architect think about first?
Maya wants to be an architect one day.
The architect used arches to let in more light.
An architect must consider safety and cost.

argue.childMeaning: To disagree with someone, or to give reasons for a view.
argue.repitchedFrom: grade 2: 'to disagree with someone and talk crossly about it' - only the quarrel sense. At this grade a writer also argues a case, which is what the unit's `justify` and `debate` need it to mean.
practiceSentences: Try not to argue about whose turn it is.
Why do the two characters argue in chapter three?
She can argue her case very clearly.
The brothers argue over small things.
Leo will argue for a longer break time.

assess.childMeaning: To judge how good, big or serious something is.
practiceSentences: The teacher will assess our projects on Friday.
How do you assess your own work?
Engineers assess the bridge every year.
Assess the damage before you start repairs.
It is hard to assess a task you have not tried.

assist.childMeaning: To help someone with a task or a job.
practiceSentences: Will you assist me with these boxes?
Who can assist the new pupil today?
Nora offered to assist with the display.
Two helpers assist at every lunchtime.
He asked a friend to assist him.

assistant.childMeaning: A person who helps someone else with their job or task.
practiceSentences: The shop assistant helped us find the size.
Who is the head teacher's assistant?
An assistant sorted the books each morning.
Leo works as an assistant at the library club.
The assistant answered every question kindly.

atmosphere.childMeaning: The layer of gases that surrounds the Earth.
atmosphere.repitchedFrom: grade 7: 'the general mood or feeling that surrounds a place or event' - the MOOD sense, in a Nature & Weather unit. This is the clearest wrong-sense case in the grade so far.
practiceSentences: The atmosphere protects us from the sun's rays.
How thick is the Earth's atmosphere?
Smoke from fires pollutes the atmosphere.
Clouds form in the lower part of the atmosphere.
Gases in the atmosphere trap some of the heat.

attempt.childMeaning: An effort to do something, which might succeed or fail.
practiceSentences: Her first attempt at the jump was very close.
How many attempts did the task take?
Make one careful attempt before asking for help.
Sami's second attempt was much better.
A brave attempt is worth more than no try.

attention.childMeaning: Careful thought, focus or notice given to something.
practiceSentences: Pay attention to the instructions.
Did the poster catch your attention?
This task needs your full attention.
He gave careful attention to every joint.
The strange noise drew our attention.

attitude.childMeaning: The way you think and feel, shown in how you act.
practiceSentences: Her positive attitude lifted the whole team.
What attitude helps you learn best?
A helpful attitude makes group work easier.
Leo changed his attitude after the talk.
Your attitude matters as much as your skill.

audio.childMeaning: Sound that has been recorded so you can listen to it.
practiceSentences: The audio was too quiet to hear properly.
Can you turn the audio up a little?
Nora recorded the audio for the class podcast.
This book comes with audio of every chapter.
Poor audio spoils an otherwise good video.

authority.childMeaning: The power to make decisions, or a group that holds it.
authority.repitchedFrom: grade 5: 'The respect or trust a person is given because of their knowledge or position' - only the personal standing. This unit sets the word beside council, official and government, where an authority is also a BODY.
practiceSentences: The head teacher has authority over the school.
Which authority looks after our local roads?
A police officer has authority to stop traffic.
She spoke with quiet authority.
The local authority repaired the broken bridge.

autobiography.childMeaning: The story of a person's life, written by that person.
autobiography.note: Written to sit against `biography`, taught in unit 1 as "written by somebody else". The pair is the point, so the fourth sentence names the contrast directly.
practiceSentences: She wrote an autobiography about her childhood.
Whose autobiography did you read?
An autobiography uses the word 'I' throughout.
An autobiography is by you; a biography is not.
His autobiography begins in a small village.

aware.childMeaning: Knowing that something exists or is happening.
aware.repitchedFrom: grade 8: 'Having knowledge or understanding of a situation or of something that is happening'.
practiceSentences: Be aware of what you eat each day.
Were you aware that the fruit had spoiled?
Amal is aware of her food allergy.
Stay aware of how your body feels.
The class became aware of the sugar in drinks.
The broken machine made an awful noise.
Was the weather awful all weekend?
An awful smell came from the drain.
She felt awful about the damaged book.
The old rope was in an awful state.

axis.childMeaning: A line that something turns around.
axis.note: The rotation sense, because the word sits beside `rotation` in this group. `axis` also names a line on a graph; that sense is not taught here.
practiceSentences: The Earth spins on its axis once a day.
Where is the axis of this wheel?
A globe turns on a tilted axis.
The axis runs from the top to the bottom.
Draw the axis through the centre.

bacteria.childMeaning: Tiny living things, too small to see, that can cause illness or help us.
bacteria.repitchedFrom: grade 6 - the same sense at 81 characters, one over this grade's cap. Its five sentences were Grade 6 too, all of them past the cap.
practiceSentences: Bacteria are far too small to see without a microscope.
Can bacteria in food make you unwell?
Washing your hands removes many bacteria.
Some bacteria help your body digest food.
Cooking meat properly kills harmful bacteria.

beneficial.childMeaning: Having a good effect on somebody or something.
practiceSentences: Fresh vegetables are beneficial to your health.
Is a short nap beneficial after lunch?
Walking daily is beneficial for the heart.
Clean water is beneficial to the whole village.
Sunlight is beneficial in small amounts.

besides.childMeaning: As well as; in addition to.
practiceSentences: Besides Nora, three others joined the debate.
Who else came besides the head teacher?
Besides being useful, the map is beautiful.
We have nothing besides these two brochures.
Besides, the meeting had already finished.

bibliography.childMeaning: A list of the books and sources used in a piece of work.
practiceSentences: Put a bibliography at the end of your report.
How many books are in your bibliography?
The bibliography lists every website used.
A bibliography shows where your facts came from.
Leo added one more book to his bibliography.

biography.childMeaning: The true story of a real person's life, written by somebody else.
biography.repitchedFrom: grade 7 - the same sense, at 86 characters.
practiceSentences: Nora read a biography of a famous doctor.
Whose biography did you choose for your project?
The biography described his childhood in detail.
A biography is written about someone, not by them.
Maya is writing a short biography of her grandmother.

boundary.childMeaning: A line that shows where one area ends and another begins.
practiceSentences: The river forms the boundary between two farms.
Where is the boundary of the school grounds?
A fence marks the boundary of the field.
The boundary is drawn clearly on the map.
Two countries share this long boundary.

brochure.childMeaning: A small booklet giving information about something.
practiceSentences: The museum brochure lists every gallery.
Did you keep the brochure from the trip?
Our class made a brochure about the town.
A brochure uses pictures as well as words.
Amal designed the cover of the brochure.

browser.childMeaning: A program you use to look at pages on the internet.
practiceSentences: Open the browser and type in the address.
Which browser is on the school computers?
The browser saved the page for later reading.
A browser shows you one webpage at a time.
Leo closed the browser when the lesson ended.

button.childMeaning: A small part that you press to make a machine or device work.
practiceSentences: Press the green button to start the machine.
Which button turns the volume down?
Amal pressed the button and the lift moved.
A red button stops the whole conveyor belt.
Do not press that button without asking first.

candidate.childMeaning: A person hoping to be chosen, such as in an election.
practiceSentences: Each candidate gave a short speech.
Which candidate will you vote for?
The candidate promised more books for the library.
Nora was a candidate for class captain.
Three candidates stood for the same position.

capable.childMeaning: Having the skill or strength to do something.
capable.repitchedFrom: grade 7: 'Having the ability, skill, or qualities needed to do something well'.
practiceSentences: The body is capable of healing small cuts.
Are you capable of running the whole distance?
A healthy heart is capable of hard work.
Sami is capable of preparing a simple meal.
Plants are capable of making their own food.

capacity.childMeaning: The amount that a container can hold.
practiceSentences: The jug has a capacity of two litres.
What is the capacity of this tank?
The hall has a capacity of two hundred.
Measure the capacity in millilitres.
A larger bottle has a greater capacity.

casual.childMeaning: Relaxed and not planned or formal.
casual.repitchedFrom: grade 8: 'Relaxed and informal, without much planning or seriousness'.
practiceSentences: We had a casual lunch in the garden.
Is this a casual meal or a special one?
A casual walk after dinner aids digestion.
Leo made a casual remark about the soup.
The picnic had a friendly, casual feel.

categorise.childMeaning: To sort things into groups by what they have in common.
practiceSentences: Categorise the books by subject, please.
How would you categorise these answers?
We categorise waste before we recycle it.
Leo tried to categorise every survey reply.
It helps to categorise facts before writing.

celebration.childMeaning: A happy time when people do something special together.
practiceSentences: The whole village joined the celebration.
What celebration is held in your country each year?
Independence Day is a national celebration.
Nora helped plan the celebration at school.
Music and food are part of every celebration.

cell.childMeaning: The smallest living part that all plants and animals are made of.
cell.note: The BIOLOGY sense, because this unit teaches it beside tissue, skeleton and reproduce. `cell` also means part of an electrical circuit, and that sense belongs to a science unit rather than a health one - the two must not share a card.
practiceSentences: Every living thing is built from at least one cell.
How small is a single blood cell?
Leo drew a plant cell in his science book.
A cell is far too small to see by eye.
Your body makes new cells every single day.

charity.childMeaning: An organisation that collects money to help others.
practiceSentences: The charity builds wells in dry villages.
Which charity will the class support?
A charity depends on the kindness of givers.
Nora raised money for a local charity.
The charity sent blankets after the flood.

circuit.childMeaning: A complete path that electricity can flow around.
practiceSentences: The bulb lit when the circuit was complete.
Why did the circuit stop working?
A broken wire leaves a gap in the circuit.
Leo built a simple circuit with a battery.
Every circuit needs a source of power.

cite.childMeaning: To name something as the source of your evidence.
practiceSentences: Always cite the book you took the fact from.
Which source will you cite in your report?
Nora forgot to cite the website she used.
You must cite evidence when you make a claim.
Cite the author's name and the page number.

clause.childMeaning: A group of words containing a verb, part of a sentence.
practiceSentences: This sentence has two clauses.
Which clause is the main one?
A clause must contain a verb.
Join the two clauses with a comma.
The second clause explains the first.

coastal.childMeaning: Close to the sea, or along the edge of the land.
coastal.repitchedFrom: grade 3: 'Something located close to the sea or along the coastline' - it explains `coastal` with `coastline`, so a reader who does not know the word learns nothing.
practiceSentences: The coastal path follows the cliffs.
Is this a coastal town?
Coastal winds are strong in winter.
Many coastal villages depend on fishing.
The coastal road was closed by the storm.

code.childMeaning: Instructions written in a special language that tell a computer what to do.
code.repitchedFrom: grade 6: 'A system of letters, numbers or symbols used to hide or send a message' - the SECRET-CODE sense. This unit sits beside robot, software and application, where code is what a program is made of.
practiceSentences: Leo wrote code to make the robot turn left.
Can you fix the mistake in this code?
The code repeats the same step ten times.
Nora learned to write code at the club.
A single wrong letter can break the whole code.

colleague.childMeaning: A person who works with you at your job.
practiceSentences: My mother met a colleague at the market.
Is he a colleague of your father?
A good colleague shares the work fairly.
Teacher Yasmin thanked a colleague for the help.
The nurse asked a colleague to check the notes.

collection.childMeaning: A group of things gathered together in one place.
practiceSentences: The museum has a fine collection of old coins.
How large is your stamp collection?
A collection of stories filled the shelf.
The school made a collection for the charity.
Amal added a shell to her collection.

combine.childMeaning: To mix two or more things together.
combine.note: Meaning kept. The Grade 5 sentences opened with writing advice - combining honesty with feeling - which teaches the word in a topic this unit is not about.
practiceSentences: Combine the blue and yellow to make green.
What happens if you combine sand and water?
We combine our pocket money to buy one gift.
Combine the two teams into a single group.
Nora will combine both lists into one.

comparison.childMeaning: Looking at two things to see how they differ.
comparison.repitchedFrom: grade 5 - the same sense at 82 characters.
practiceSentences: Make a comparison between the two poems.
What comparison can you draw here?
The comparison showed one clear difference.
A comparison helps you notice detail.
Her comparison of the towns was very fair.

compass.childMeaning: A tool with a needle that always points north.
practiceSentences: Use the compass to find your way home.
Which way is north on this compass?
The compass needle swung round slowly.
A compass is useful when there is no path.
She checked the compass before setting off.

competition.childMeaning: An event where people try their best to win.
practiceSentences: Leo entered the spelling competition.
Who won the drawing competition last year?
The competition was fair and well organised.
A friendly competition brought the class together.
Every competition needs clear rules.

complain.childMeaning: To say that you are unhappy about something.
practiceSentences: Do not complain until you have tried it.
Why did the neighbours complain about the noise?
She went to complain about the broken gate.
It is better to act than to complain.
Sami did not complain once during the long walk.

compose.childMeaning: To write or put together a piece of music or writing.
practiceSentences: She will compose a song for the concert.
Can you compose a short poem about rain?
He took an hour to compose the letter.
Compose your sentence before you write it down.
The class composed a tune together.

concentrate.childMeaning: To give all your attention to one thing.
practiceSentences: Concentrate on the road while you cycle.
Can you concentrate with music playing?
It is hard to concentrate in a noisy room.
Nora had to concentrate to hear the faint sound.
Concentrate on one question at a time.

concerning.childMeaning: To do with, or on the subject of, something.
practiceSentences: A notice concerning the workshop was posted.
Have you news concerning the delivery?
He asked a question concerning the design.
The report concerning safety was very clear.
Rules concerning the machines are on the wall.

conclude.childMeaning: To finish something, or to decide after thinking.
practiceSentences: We will conclude the meeting at four o'clock.
What did the class conclude from the survey?
The report will conclude with a recommendation.
From the evidence, we conclude that walking is common.
Leo tried to conclude his speech with a question.

condition.childMeaning: The state that a person or a thing is in.
condition.repitchedFrom: grade 5 - the same sense at 89 characters, which is past this grade's cap.
practiceSentences: The patient's condition improved by morning.
What condition is the fruit in?
Asthma is a condition that affects breathing.
The food was in poor condition after the heat.
Doctor Sarah checked his condition each day.

confidence.childMeaning: The feeling of believing in yourself and your abilities.
practiceSentences: Practice gave her confidence before the concert.
How can we build confidence in a shy pupil?
His confidence grew with every attempt.
Confidence is quiet, not loud.
Nora spoke with confidence to the whole school.

confirm.childMeaning: To say or show that something is definitely true.
practiceSentences: Please confirm that you will attend.
Can you confirm the time of the match?
The test will confirm our first result.
Leo rang to confirm the booking.
Two witnesses confirm what happened.

conflict.childMeaning: A serious disagreement between people or groups.
conflict.repitchedFrom: grade 5: 'A struggle or problem between characters that needs to be faced and solved' - the LITERARY sense, meant for analysing a story. This unit is about how people actually treat one another, where a conflict is a disagreement.
practiceSentences: The conflict began over a misunderstanding.
How can we settle this conflict fairly?
Talking calmly can end a conflict quickly.
The two families resolved their conflict.
Conflict is easier to prevent than to fix.

confusion.childMeaning: Not being able to understand what is happening.
confusion.repitchedFrom: grade 6: 'A state of being unclear, uncertain, or unable to understand something properly' - three near-synonyms where one clause does the work.
practiceSentences: There was confusion about the meeting time.
What caused all this confusion?
Her confusion cleared once she read the note.
Confusion spread when the lights went out.
Ask a question to avoid confusion later.
It rained; consequently, the match was moved.
She practised daily and, consequently, improved.
Consequently, the plan had to change.
The road flooded; consequently, we walked.
Consequently, our results were much clearer.

conservation.childMeaning: Looking after nature so it is not damaged or used up.
practiceSentences: Conservation protects the forest and its animals.
What can our class do for conservation?
Water conservation matters in a dry season.
The park has a conservation area for birds.
Nora joined a conservation club after school.

consider.childMeaning: To think carefully about something before deciding.
practiceSentences: Consider both routes before you choose.
Did you consider asking for help?
We must consider the cost of the trip.
Nora asked us to consider her idea.
Consider how others will feel about it.

considering.childMeaning: Taking something into account before you judge.
considering.repitchedFrom: grade 8: 'Thinking carefully about something before making a decision' - that is the VERB `consider`, which is already a Core word in unit 5. This word sits in the linking group, where `considering the rain` means taking the rain into account.
practiceSentences: Considering the rain, the trip went well.
Considering her age, she runs very fast.
The map is clear, considering how old it is.
Considering the distance, we arrived early.
Considering everything, the plan worked.

constitution.childMeaning: A set of rules that explains how a country or group works.
constitution.note: Meaning kept in a slightly shorter form; three Grade 5 sentences ran past this grade's cap.
practiceSentences: Our club's constitution gives every member a vote.
Who wrote the country's first constitution?
The constitution protects the rights of citizens.
The council wrote a short constitution.
Changing a constitution takes a long time.

construct.childMeaning: To build something by putting parts together.
practiceSentences: The class will construct a model bridge.
How long did it take to construct the shed?
Workers construct the wall one row at a time.
Leo helped construct a shelter from branches.
You construct a sentence from separate words.

context.childMeaning: The situation or background that helps you understand something.
practiceSentences: Read the whole page to find the context.
What context does the first chapter give?
Context helps you guess an unknown word.
Without context, the quotation is confusing.

contraction.childMeaning: A short form of two words, written with an apostrophe.
